entries.reason: Reference releases the IOMemoryDescriptor at 5084 on the wireMemory: failure path, then the guard at 5088-5092 (cmpwi cr1,r31,0 / beq cr1,loc_1428) tests r31, which still holds the released descriptor - nothing between 5084 and 5088 clears it. The path therefore falls into 5096-5156 and sends executeRequest:ioMemoryDescriptor:, unwireMemory and a second release to a freed object (IOMemoryDescriptor.h:132-134: -release is a real refcount release; wireMemory: fails on client-supplied addresses, so the path is client-reachable). We clear the descriptor after releasing it so the block is skipped.

entries.reason: IORequestNotifyForClientTask: the reference's two early failure paths (addresses 8592-8604 and 8656-8680) clear the notifClients slot they reserved but never undo the notifClientCnt++ at 8548-8552, although the third failure path at 8820-8836 does. Every ipc_object_copyout_compat or IOReferenceClientTask failure therefore leaves notifClientCnt permanently above the number of live entries, and _io_task_notification trusts that count both as a loop bound (7848-7856, 8164-8172) and as its own should-I-still-be-running test (7816-7824, 7956-7968). Our source decrements on both paths. Apple's defect recorded, not reproduced, per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-kernel-pci-pcmcia-reconstruction.md:968.
